category_title: Limited-proficiency students requiring significant L1 support
student_description: This student has lower English (L2) proficiency and frequently relies on their native Chinese (L1) to answer content questions in CLIL lessons. While they understand the academic concepts, they lack the English academic vocabulary to express them and become frustrated when forced to produce it on the spot. They uniquely need implicit L2 recasting, morphological breakdown of terms, and structured preparation time to bridge the gap between content knowledge and L2 expression.

criteria.rationale: The student lacks the foundational academic English required for CLIL, necessitating dedicated, intensive language support outside of standard content lessons.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes small-class or intensive bridging interventions specifically focused on developing English academic language proficiency.

criteria.rationale: Excessive reliance on L1 (e.g., 80% of the time) prevents the student from learning how to express content in English.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes a deliberate strategy to gradually decrease the use of L1 instruction and increase L2 exposure over time.
